extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, and professionals seeking an encyclopedic overview of television history, technology, standards, and regulation
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic overview of television covering its history, technical formats and standards, regulatory/codes references, and related technologies. The page surveys inventions, patents, broadcast standards, video/audio formats, and broadcasting policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Commercial Communications Code
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as part of broadcasting regulation (cited in context of 'BAI launches Revised Broadcasting Codes'). Indicates an authoritative code governing commercial communications; the page notes it alongside a Children's Commercial Communications Code and links to archived versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's Commercial Communications Code
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced together with the General Commercial Communications Code as regulatory material used by the Broadcasting Authority of Ireland in revised broadcasting codes; implies special rules for commercials targeting children.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Television System Committee transmission standards for colour television
rubrics_metrics.description: National Television System Committee (1951–1953) reports and petition for adoption of transmission standards for colour television before the Federal Communications Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as the authoritative body/reporting process that produced transmission standards and petitioned the FCC for colour television standards; used as historical and technical benchmark for system adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video formats and television line systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists analog and digital video formats and line systems (e.g., 405 lines, 525 lines System M, 625 lines System B/C/G/H/I, 819 lines, 1125 lines, HD-MAC, and digital formats such as SDTV/HDTV/UHDTV including 480i/576i/720p/1080i/1080p/4K/8K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates common broadcast and display formats used historically and in present-day television; serves as a taxonomy for technical compatibility and production/encoding decisions (choice of format affects resolution, scanning method, and broadcast compatibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour television systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Colour systems named and listed (NTSC, NTSC-J, Clear-Vision, PAL, PAL-M, PAL-N, PALplus, SECAM, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the major colour-encoding systems historically used in broadcast television; selection of a colour system affects transmitter/receiver compatibility and standards compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Video Broadcasting (DVB) – BPSK modulation implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Digital Video Broadcasting (DVB); Implementation of Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK) modulation in DVB satellite transmission systems" (ETSI report TR 101 198).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical reference on modulation implementation for DVB satellite systems; relevant to engineers implementing or evaluating DVB satellite transmissions and compliance with ETSI recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: DCT source coding for HDTV
rubrics_metrics.description: "DCT source coding and current implementations for HDTV" (EBU Technical Review article).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform) source coding approaches and implementations for HDTV, informing decisions about compression, image quality, and encoder implementation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlaced vs progressive scan signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about interlaced and progressive scan signals (referenced guidance/link).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes scanning methods (interlaced vs progressive); important for production, display, standards conversion, and perceived motion/clarity. Page references explanatory resources on their differences and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captioning, teletext and hidden signals (accessibility and metadata)
rubrics_metrics.description: Captioning, Teletext, VBI, AFD, Broadcast flag, and other hidden signals/metadata are listed among audio/hidden signals and broadcast features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These features provide accessibility (captioning), ancillary data (teletext, VBI), and signaling (AFD, broadcast flag) for receivers and services. Inclusion and correct encoding of these signals are criteria for regulatory compliance and accessibility best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast‑safe / Standards conversion / Test card
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical issues section including '14:9 compromise', 'Broadcast-safe', 'Digital cinema (DCI)', 'Display motion blur', 'Standards conversion', and 'Test card'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers practices and technical checks to ensure content is compatible with broadcast systems and displays (broadcast-safe levels, aspect-ratio compromises, test cards for calibration) and the processes for converting between different standards/formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installing consumer‑owned antennas and satellite dishes (FCC guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Installing Consumer-Owned Antennas and Satellite Dishes" (FCC) — guidance referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical/regulatory guidance from the FCC on installation of consumer antennas/dishes; relevant to compliance with local regulations, safety, and correct reception practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards, modulation and transport technologies for digital television
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentions of MPEG-2, MPEG-4, MPEG-4 AVC, ATSC, DVB, ISDB, DTMB, AVS, HEVC/HEVC variants, and related transport technologies and codecs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates the major codecs and broadcast standards used globally; selection affects compression efficiency, compatibility with receivers/set-top boxes, and regulatory compliance (e.g., national standard adoption).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory and market reports (OFCOM, House of Commons Library, industry groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: References to reports such as 'Video on demand: Research Paper 94/68' (House of Commons Library), OFCOM's Global TV Market Report, and industry market-share/regulatory documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reports provide metrics, policy guidance, and regulatory context used to evaluate market, policy decisions, and compliance; they serve as sources when assessing broadcasting policy or market trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast metadata and electronic programme guide (EPG)
rubrics_metrics.description: References to EPG and related on-screen metadata (listed under Hidden signals and Audio/Hidden signals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPG and metadata are technical/regulatory features that enable programme discovery and interactive services; correct population and signaling of metadata is part of service quality and compliance.
